title: NLP Generation Metrics: BLEU, ROUGE & Beyond
interviewAnswer: BLEU measures n-gram precision with brevity handling, ROUGE emphasizes overlap/recall; both are limited proxies for semantic quality. Modern evaluation often combines task metrics, learned metrics and human judgment.
keyPoints: Lexical overlap can punish valid paraphrases.
Human/LLM evaluation needs rubrics and reliability checks.
why: NLP Generation Metrics: BLEU, ROUGE & Beyond is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
deepDive: BLEU measures n-gram precision with brevity handling, ROUGE emphasizes overlap/recall; both are limited proxies for semantic quality. Modern evaluation often combines task metrics, learned metrics and human judgment. Lexical overlap can punish valid paraphrases. Human/LLM evaluation needs rubrics and reliability checks. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: A summarizer can be factually wrong while achieving decent ROUGE due to overlapping words.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.
followUps: What assumptions or limitations does NLP Generation Metrics: BLEU, ROUGE & Beyond have?
How would you validate NLP Generation Metrics: BLEU, ROUGE & Beyond on a real dataset?
production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.
